So a dark-mode user of a server-rendered page sees the light render until the app hydrates. To avoid a light flash, give the page a dark background with a `prefers-color-scheme` media query in its CSS.

---

# `AccessibilityInfo`

Reads the accessibility settings of the user, announces text to screen readers, and moves focus.

```tsx
import { AccessibilityInfo } from 'react-native'

AccessibilityInfo.announceForAccessibility('Message sent')
```

## Settings

The browser shows some settings to a page through CSS media queries. Those are live: each `is…Enabled()` reads the current value, and each change event fires when the user changes the setting.

| Method                                                                                                      | On the web                                                                                |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `isReduceMotionEnabled()`                                                                                   | `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`. Event: `reduceMotionChanged`.                           |
| `isReduceTransparencyEnabled()`                                                                             | `prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce`. Event: `reduceTransparencyChanged`.               |
| `isInvertColorsEnabled()`                                                                                   | `inverted-colors: inverted`. Event: `invertColorsChanged`.                                |
| `isHighTextContrastEnabled()`, `isDarkerSystemColorsEnabled()`                                              | `prefers-contrast: more`. Events: `highTextContrastChanged`, `darkerSystemColorsChanged`. |
| `prefersCrossFadeTransitions()`                                                                             | `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.                                                         |
| `isScreenReaderEnabled()`, `isAccessibilityServiceEnabled()`, `isBoldTextEnabled()`, `isGrayscaleEnabled()` | `false`. A browser doesn't tell a page about these. Their events never fire.              |
| `getRecommendedTimeoutMillis(timeout)`                                                                      | Returns `timeout` unchanged.                                                              |

Don't build a feature only for screen reader users on `isScreenReaderEnabled()`. On the web it's always `false`.

`addEventListener(eventName, handler)` returns `{ remove() }`, as on native.

## Announcements

| Method                                                        | On the web                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `announceForAccessibility(text)`                              | Writes the text to a hidden `aria-live="polite"` region, so a screen reader reads it when it's idle.               |
| `announceForAccessibilityWithOptions(text, { queue: false })` | Uses `aria-live="assertive"`, so a screen reader reads it at once.                                                 |
| `addEventListener('announcementFinished', handler)`           | Fires on the next frame, with `{ announcement, success: true }`. The browser doesn't report when the reading ends. |

All announcements share one live region. The same text twice in a row is read twice.

## Focus

| Method                                     | On the web                                             |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `setAccessibilityFocus(element)`           | Moves keyboard and screen reader focus to the element. |
| `sendAccessibilityEvent(element, 'focus')` | The same. Other event types do nothing.                |

Pass the element itself, for example the ref of a `View`. A node handle number does nothing on the web. The element must be able to take focus: give a `View` `tabIndex={-1}` so that it can, without joining the tab order.

---

# `I18nManager`

Right-to-left layout. On the web, the direction comes from the document: the `dir` attribute or the CSS `direction` of `<html>`.

```tsx
import { I18nManager } from 'react-native'

const arrow = I18nManager.isRTL ? '←' : '→'
```

| Member                                                               | On the web                                                                                                          |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `I18nManager.isRTL`                                                  | `true` when the document direction is right-to-left. It reads the current direction each time.                      |
| `I18nManager.forceRTL(force)`                                        | Sets `dir="rtl"` on `<html>` at once. On native it waits for a restart. `false` clears the attribute.               |
| `I18nManager.allowRTL(allow)`                                        | `false` makes `isRTL` report `false`. The browser still lays out the page from `dir`, so the layout doesn't change. |
| `I18nManager.getConstants()`                                         | `{ isRTL, doLeftAndRightSwapInRTL, localeIdentifier }`. `localeIdentifier` is `navigator.language`.                 |
| `I18nManager.swapLeftAndRightInRTL(swap)`, `doLeftAndRightSwapInRTL` | Stores and reports the flag. It has no effect on styles yet. See below.                                             |

On the server, `isRTL` is `false`.

## Left and right styles

On native, with the default `doLeftAndRightSwapInRTL` of `true`, `marginLeft`, `paddingLeft`, `left`, and their right partners swap in a right-to-left layout. On the web they don't swap yet: they stay on the physical side.

For styles that must follow the direction, use the start and end props: `marginStart`, `paddingEnd`, `start`, and the others. They work the same on every platform. See [Right-to-left](https://rootnative.github.io/web/styles#right-to-left).

---

# `BackHandler`

The browser has no hardware back button, and the history of the page belongs to your router. So on the web, back handlers register and remove as on native, but never fire.

| Member                                                     | On the web                                                  |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `BackHandler.addEventListener('hardwareBackPress', fn)`    | Registers `fn` and returns `{ remove() }`. `fn` never runs. |
| `BackHandler.removeEventListener('hardwareBackPress', fn)` | Removes `fn`.                                               |
| `BackHandler.exitApp()`                                    | Does nothing. A page can't close a tab that it didn't open. |

To act on the browser's back button, use the history API of your router.

---

# `PixelRatio`

The pixel density of the screen and the font scale of the user.

| Member                                       | On the web                                                                     |
| -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `PixelRatio.get()`                           | `devicePixelRatio`. A browser zoom changes it.                                 |
| `PixelRatio.getFontScale()`                  | The root font size divided by 16, the user's font-size setting in the browser. |
| `PixelRatio.getPixelSizeForLayoutSize(size)` | `size` times the ratio, rounded to a whole device pixel.                       |
| `PixelRatio.roundToNearestPixel(size)`       | `size` rounded to the nearest device pixel.                                    |
| `PixelRatio.startDetecting()`                | Does nothing. The browser reports the ratio by itself.                         |

On the server, `get()` and `getFontScale()` return `1`.

---

# `processColor`

Turns a color into the number that React Native passes to native code. Libraries call it. An app seldom needs it.

```tsx
import { processColor } from 'react-native'

processColor('red') // 4294901760, which is 0xffff0000
```

| Input                                 | Result                                      |
| ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| A color that React Native can parse   | An unsigned 32-bit ARGB integer, as on iOS. |
| A color that React Native can't parse | `null`.                                     |
| `null` or `undefined`                 | The same value.                             |

Android returns the same bits as a signed integer. On the web, the number is always unsigned.

---

# `PanResponder`

Tracks a drag with the React Native gesture state. On the web it runs on pointer events, so it works with a mouse, a pen, and touch.

```tsx
import { useRef } from 'react'
import { PanResponder, View } from 'react-native'

export function Draggable() {
  const pan = useRef(
    PanResponder.create({
      onStartShouldSetPanResponder: () => true,
      onPanResponderMove: (event, gesture) => {
        // gesture.dx and gesture.dy since the grant
      },
    }),
  ).current

  return <View {...pan.panHandlers} style={{ width: 80, height: 80, touchAction: 'none' }} />
}
```

> **WARNING: Set `touchAction` on a touch screen**
>
> Put `touchAction: 'none'` in the style of the element, or `'pan-y'` for a horizontal drag inside a vertical scroll. Without it, the browser scrolls the page instead of giving your responder the gesture. The responder can't set it for you: the browser reads it before the gesture starts.

## Handlers

`panHandlers` are six pointer handlers: `onPointerDown`, `onPointerMove`, `onPointerUp`, `onPointerCancel`, and the two capture variants. Spread them on a `View`.

When the responder takes the gesture, the element captures the pointer, so the gesture continues outside the element.

## Negotiation

One responder holds a gesture at a time, as on native. The should-set callbacks with `Capture` run from the parent to the child. The others run from the child to the parent.

When a responder asks for a gesture that another one holds, the holder's `onPanResponderTerminationRequest` decides. `true` (the default) moves the gesture: the holder gets `onPanResponderTerminate`, and the new one gets `onPanResponderGrant`. `false` keeps it, and the asker gets `onPanResponderReject`.

## Gesture state

| Field                 | On the web                                                                           |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `dx`, `dy`            | The distance since the grant, in CSS pixels, from the center of the active pointers. |
| `vx`, `vy`            | The speed, in pixels per millisecond.                                                |
| `x0`, `y0`            | The page position at the grant.                                                      |
| `moveX`, `moveY`      | The latest page position.                                                            |
| `numberActiveTouches` | The pointers that are down on the element.                                           |
| `stateID`             | A new number for each gesture.                                                       |

A pointer that joins or leaves doesn't move the gesture. The event's `nativeEvent` is the pointer event with `touches`, `changedTouches`, `identifier`, `locationX`, `locationY`, `pageX`, `pageY`, `timestamp`, and `force` (the pen pressure) added.

## Not on the web

- `onShouldBlockNativeResponder` is ignored. The web has no native responder to block.
- `getInteractionHandle()` returns `null`.

---

# `usePressability`

The press handling behind [`Pressable`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/pressable), as a hook. Use it to build your own pressable component.

```tsx
import { useMemo } from 'react'
import { usePressability, View } from 'react-native'

export function Card({ onPress, children }) {
  const config = useMemo(() => ({ onPress }), [onPress])
  const handlers = usePressability(config)
  return (
    <View {...handlers} role="button">
      {children}
    </View>
  )
}
```

Memoize the config. A new config object on each render makes the hook configure itself again.

## Handlers

On the web, the hook returns pointer, keyboard, and focus handlers, not the responder handlers of native: `onPointerDown`, `onPointerUp`, `onPointerMove`, `onPointerCancel`, `onPointerEnter`, `onPointerLeave`, `onKeyDown`, `onKeyUp`, `onClick`, `onContextMenu`, `onFocus`, and `onBlur`. Spread them on a `View`. Their identity never changes.

A `null` config returns `null` and sets up nothing. The hook sets up when a config arrives.

## Config

| Field                                                                 | On the web                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `onPress`, `onPressIn`, `onPressOut`, `onLongPress`, `onPressMove`    | As on [`Pressable`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/pressable#how-a-press-works). `onPress` gets the pointer up event, or the click event for a keyboard or assistive technology press. `preventDefault()` on it cancels the click. |
| `onHoverIn`, `onHoverOut`, `delayHoverIn`, `delayHoverOut`            | A mouse or a pen. Touch doesn't hover.                                                                                                                                                               |
| `onFocus`, `onBlur`                                                   | Focus events of the element.                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `delayPressIn`, `delayPressOut`, `delayLongPress`, `minPressDuration` | As on native. `delayLongPress` defaults to 500 ms, and `minPressDuration` to 130 ms.                                                                                                                 |
| `disabled`                                                            | Stops every press.                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `hitSlop`, `pressRectOffset`                                          | Grow the area where a release still presses. `hitSlop` doesn't grow the hit area here: `Pressable` does that with CSS.                                                                               |
| `cancelable`                                                          | Accepted. `Pressable` turns `false` into `touch-action: none`. With the hook, set `touchAction` in the style yourself.                                                                               |
| `android_disableSound`, `blockNativeResponder`                        | Native only. Accepted and ignored.                                                                                                                                                                   |
